open_obligations: Check which elements of Khan et al.'s protocol (rounds, turn order, quote verification) are actually kept
Check whether Lang et al.'s debaters, two instances of a large pretrained model, differ in kind from the 'two expert models' in Khan et al.'s passage
in.other_title: Lang et al. follow Khan et al.'s assigned-answer LLM debate to extract information for training better weak models
in.rationale: The passage says the protocol follows Michael et al., Khan et al. and Kenton et al. but does not itself state what is different. Comparing the passages, Khan et al.'s debaters generate their arguments simultaneously and after N rounds a judge reads the transcript, whereas Lang et al.'s debaters take turns and the trustworthy information from the debate is used to help train a better weak model, which matches EXTENDS; whether Lang et al. use a judge is open.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Assigned-role, fixed-turn LLM debate used as an information source; holds where the debate output feeds weak-model training rather than a judge verdict

text: The authors define debate as a protocol in which two expert models argue for opposing answers over a pre-determined number of rounds N; in each round the debaters see previous arguments and simultaneously generate new ones, and after N rounds a judge reads the transcript and tries to choose the correct answer. The adversarial character comes from each debater presenting arguments for why the opponent's claims are false.
title: Fixed-round LLM debate: simultaneous opposing arguments, judge reads the final transcript
